messages.subject: How to extract current iteration
parts:
This should be a simple question, I think. How can we extract the current iteration number inside a user-defined sampler?

I want to implement a user-defined sampler ever X iterations. I want to do this because the default sampler does not allow the posterior to be fully explored for this particular model. I have an alternative sampler that does not have this problem, but it is much more computationally costly. However, I only need to use it every once in a while to make sure all disjunct areas of the posterior are sampled. My plan is to recreate both the Nimble default update and the second update inside a user-defined sampler and only use the second one every X iterations. To do this, I need to know which iteration we are currently on.

Thanks,

Ben Augustine

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: How to extract current iteration
parts:
Easiest way:

In the setup code of your sampler function, include:
iterationNumber <- 0

In the run function of your sampler, include:
iterationNumber <<- iterationNumber + 1    ## note the double-assignment arrow, which is necessary
if(iterationNumber %% [how often you want this sampler to operate, e.g. 100 for every 100 MCMC iterations] == 0) {
   ## code for your custom (computationally expensive) sampling algorithm
}

In the reset methods of your sampler, include:
methods = list(
   reset = function() {
      iterationNumber <<- 0
      ## plus anything else you need to reset to a base state, here
   }
)

That should do the trick.
